purpose: Close ASVS V11.2.4 at its cause: give the unknown-account login branch the same bcrypt work factor as the known-account branch, by giving the platform one owner for password hashing.
requiredInvariants: No cryptography is written; bcryptjs, already a dependency, keeps doing the work.
The bcrypt cost is declared exactly once and every writer and dummy hash derives from that declaration.
The branch between the known-account and unknown-account paths lives inside the shared module, so a caller cannot skip bcrypt for a missing user.
The cost stays at 12 and never drops; this task is about parity, not about raising the factor.
Stored password hashes are not rewritten and existing passwords keep verifying.
A decision whose evidence this change invalidates is rewritten in the same PR, never left to rust.
Regression tests fail if the dummy and stored costs diverge, or if any file outside the owning module chooses a cost.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: bcrypt.getRounds(DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH) equals the cost used to write stored passwords, asserted by test.
The unknown-account path is proved to compare against a hash of that same cost without a timing assertion.
A test fails if any file outside the owning module passes a numeric cost to bcrypt.
Both mutations were verified to turn the suite red before the fix was accepted.
V11.2.4 moves from FAIL to PASS with new self-revoking conditions, and V11.4.2 keeps PASS with conditions that match the new code.
The evidence gate rejects 0 decisions at the head.
tsc --noEmit is clean and the auth and deals suites pass.
